quickAnswer: Dover is almost all detached houses on oil: 95.8% of homes are single-family detached, the highest share of the 50 towns we serve, and fuel oil heats 71.4% of occupied homes (2nd-highest). Heating decisions here are mostly made house by house.
body: ## Nearly every home is a detached house

According to the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), 1,872 of Dover's 1,955 housing units (95.8%) are single-family detached houses. No other town on our list has a larger share of detached houses, and the middle town sits at 76.7%. Only 25 units (1.3%) sit in multi-unit buildings, the lowest share of all 50, and renters hold just 110 households (5.8%), 48th of 50. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $1,152,400, 4th-highest of the 50.

Detached houses on their own lots usually mean a heating job of one boiler or furnace, one tank and one set of pipes or ducts, with no shared building system to coordinate. Wikipedia notes that almost all residential zoning in Dover requires 1 acre or larger, which is worth keeping in mind when an outdoor unit, a fuel tank or a new line has to be placed on a property.
## Oil, and then more oil

Fuel oil or kerosene heats 1,347 of Dover's 1,887 occupied homes (71.4%), the 2nd-highest share among the 50 towns and almost twice the 36.5% of the middle town. Utility gas heats only 9.0%, 47th of 50. When an oil boiler wears out, the choice is between another oil system and a switch, and a heat pump that heats and cools is the usual alternative to weigh. The heating load, assessed first, sets the size either way.
The other fuels are on the [heating page](/cities/dover/heating-installation-repair), and the electric side of the story is on the [heat pump page](/cities/dover/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

The age mix is wide. The median Dover home was built in 1972, and 251 units (12.8%) date from 1939 or earlier, which ranks 34th of 50. Another 654 (33.5%) went up between 1960 and 1979. A house from 1939 or earlier and one from the 1960 to 1979 band call for different decisions about insulation, boilers and ducts, and the heating load of each is the thing to measure.
## Snow, old roads and a house from 1777

Dover was first recorded as settled in 1640, became the Springfield Parish of Dedham in 1748, was incorporated as District Dedham in 1784 and became a town in 1836. It sits about 15 miles southwest of downtown Boston on the south bank of the Charles River, covers 15.4 square miles and is bordered by Natick, Wellesley, Needham, Westwood, Walpole, Medfield and Sherborn. Wikipedia says that as recently as the early 1960s, 75% of the annual town budget went to snow removal, because only one and a half miles of the town's roads are state highway.

The Benjamin Caryl House at 107 Dedham St. dates from about 1777, and the Dover Historical Society has operated it since 1920. Wikipedia's list of historic sites also includes the Elm Bank Horticulture Center (1876). The Sawin Building was dedicated on May 14, 1907. The Caryl Elementary School was gutted by fire in 1970, rebuilt, closed in 2001 and is now a community center. At the newer end, 234 units (12.0%) have been built since 2010, which ranks 9th of 50.
## Which utility serves your address

Dover's electric utility is not confirmed in our records, so none is named here. Heat pump rebates run through the utility that serves a given address, and the right program is worth checking before you buy. The Mass Save rebate details are on the heat pump page.
## Dover at a glance

| --- | --- |

| Single-family detached homes | 95.8% (1st of 50) |
| Heated with fuel oil | 71.4% (2nd of 50) |
| Renter households | 5.8% (48th of 50) |
| Median year homes were built | 1972 |
| Median value of owner-occupied homes | $1,152,400 |

faq.q: My Dover house runs on oil. Is a heat pump realistic?
faq.a: Often it is, but it depends on the house. A heat pump both heats and cools, and a whole-home Mass Save rebate may be available if the home is weatherized and the serving utility takes part. With 71.4% of Dover homes on oil, many owners are asking. A heating load assessment gives an oil replacement and a heat pump the same starting point.

faq.q: Why does a large detached house need a load assessment?
faq.a: Size alone does not set the equipment. Insulation, windows, air leakage and layout all change how much heat a house needs. With 95.8% of Dover homes detached, each one is individual. Oversized equipment tends to cycle on and off, and undersized equipment struggles in January, so the load is assessed before a system is quoted.

faq.q: Does a gas or propane boiler swap in Dover need a permit?
faq.a: A licensed plumber or gas fitter has to file the gas permit in Massachusetts, and a boiler or furnace swap normally ends with an inspection. The town's building department can say how it handles replacements. Ask your installer who is filing before the old unit comes out.

faq.q: Which utility's heat pump rebate applies in Dover?
faq.a: That depends on the utility that serves your address, and we have not confirmed it for the whole town. Your electric bill names the utility; its heat pump program is the next thing to look up. If it is a Mass Save sponsor, the whole-home rebate described on the heat pump page is the place to start. Confirm at masssave.com.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Past oil, Dover has 229 homes on bottled or tank gas (12.1%, 3rd of 50) and 169 on utility gas. Propane and oil each bring their own tank and delivery questions, and a new gas furnace or boiler normally needs a permit.
body: ## The fuels after oil

The ACS 2022 counts 229 Dover homes (12.1%) on bottled or tank gas, which ranks 3rd of 50, and 169 (9.0%) on utility gas, 47th. A further 83 homes use another fuel or coal, and electricity heats 59. Oil still leads by a wide margin, but replacing a propane system is a different job from replacing an oil one: a propane boiler or furnace is a gas appliance, so a new one normally needs a permit and a final inspection.

Only a licensed plumber or gas fitter may pull a gas permit in Massachusetts. Ask whoever will do the work to name the person filing it, and check with the town's building department about tanks and venting.
## Age and equipment

Dover's largest age band is 654 housing units (33.5%) built between 1960 and 1979, and the median home dates to 1972. A further 188 units (9.6%) date from 1940 to 1959. A boiler or furnace in a house this old may already have been replaced. When a repair bill starts to approach the cost of new equipment, pricing a replacement can make sense.
## Tanks and deliveries

Oil and propane both arrive by delivery into a tank, so a replacement decision includes the tank itself: its age, its location and whether it suits the new equipment. A new burner on an old tank is not always the best use of money, and the reverse can also be true.
## Winter on a large property

According to Wikipedia, almost all of Dover's residential zoning requires 1 acre or larger, and large detached houses on big lots can have long pipe or duct runs to far corners. Zone control and correct sizing can matter more in a big house. Mass HVAC gives a free written estimate before work starts and takes emergency calls 24/7 at (508) 786-8755.

faq.q: Does swapping a propane boiler differ from swapping an oil boiler?
faq.a: Yes. Propane equipment is a gas appliance, so a new unit normally brings a permit and a final inspection handled by a licensed plumber or gas fitter. Oil brings its own tank and chimney questions. In Dover 229 occupied homes use bottled or tank gas, so the propane route is familiar here.

faq.q: Who answers a no-heat call in Dover?
faq.a: Mass HVAC does, at (508) 786-8755, any hour of the day. With 71.4% of Dover homes on oil, it helps to say whether the tank has fuel, along with the age of the system and what happened. A tripped breaker or a thermostat setting is worth checking before the call.

faq.q: What counts as another fuel or coal in the Dover figures?
faq.a: The Census groups 83 occupied Dover homes under another fuel or coal and does not say which fuels they are. If your house is in that group, the first step is to identify the system and how its fuel arrives, since that decides the permit, the storage and the replacement options.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Nearly all Dover homes are detached, so cooling jobs are mostly single houses with their own outdoor unit. Ducted central air and ductless mini-splits are both options; 20.6% of units date from 2000 or later and may already have ducts.
body: ## Detached houses and where the outdoor unit goes

In the ACS 2022, 402 Dover housing units (20.6%) date from 2000 or later. Newer houses are more likely to have been built with ductwork for central air, though not all are. Many older homes were built without central air, and in a town with a median build year of 1972 it is worth looking at the existing ducts before choosing between a ducted system and ductless heads.

A detached house usually does not have to share a wall, courtyard or roof with a neighbor, so an outdoor condenser can often go on the ground beside the house. Wikipedia notes residential zoning of 1 acre or larger across almost all the town, which may leave room to site a unit away from windows and bedrooms. Noise and clearance still matter, so the placement is part of the plan.
## Few shared buildings

Dover has 58 attached townhouse units (3.0%) and only 25 units in multi-unit buildings (1.3%), the lowest share of the 50 towns. Association rules and shared roofs are less likely to limit a cooling plan here than in a town of condos.
## Ducted or ductless

A ducted system cools the whole house through the existing supply and return runs if they are the right size. A ductless mini-split cools by zone, which suits additions, finished attics or rooms the main system does not reach. Mini-splits also heat, which is covered on the [heat pump page](/cities/dover/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## Sizing for summer

A cooling unit that is too big switches off before it has dried the air, while a unit sized too small runs on and on. Sun exposure, insulation and window area all feed into the sizing. Air conditioning work covers homes and businesses.

faq.q: Can I add cooling to a Dover house with no ducts?
faq.a: Yes. A mini-split needs a small wall opening and a refrigerant line to each indoor head, and the layout sets the head count. Dover's median house dates to 1972, and a house without ducts can avoid opening walls to run them. Each head can be set for its own room, so rooms in little use need not be cooled.

faq.q: Is a newer Dover house likely to have ducts already?
faq.a: More likely than an older one, but not guaranteed. A house built in 2000 or later may have ducts sized for central cooling, or it may have been built with baseboard or radiators and no ducts at all. Look at the house itself before deciding between ducted and ductless cooling.

faq.q: How much room does an outdoor condenser need in Dover?
faq.a: The unit needs open air around it and clear access for service. With zoning of 1 acre or larger across almost all of town, per Wikipedia, many properties may have room to keep a condenser away from bedroom windows and the neighbors' boundary. The town's building department can say whether any setback rules apply.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Only 59 Dover homes (3.1%) heat with electricity, the lowest share of the 50 towns, while oil heats most. The rebate path depends on which utility serves your address, and Dover's utility is not confirmed here, so read it off your bill.
body: ## No named utility, so check the bill

This page leaves Dover's electric utility unnamed because it is unconfirmed, and your electric bill settles the question. A municipal name there means Mass Save generally covers only gas-heated homes (gas from a Mass Save sponsor), with the utility's own program for the rest. If a Mass Save sponsor is named, the whole-home air source rebate for 2026 pays $2,650 per ton to a $8,500 cap after weatherization. The rest of the terms are on the [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## The least electric town on our list

The ACS 2022 puts electric heat in 59 of Dover's 1,887 occupied homes (3.1%), 50th of 50 and far below the 10.1% of the middle town. Oil heats 1,347 and bottled gas 229, with utility gas at 169. For most owners the starting point is a fuel-burning system, and a heat pump that heats and cools is a significant change best made after a full heating load assessment.
## Weatherization against Dover's age bands

Construction from 2000 on clears the weatherization test by age, and Dover has 402 such units (20.6%). At the other end, 1,093 units (55.9%) predate 1980, led by 654 from 1960 to 1979. Those owners may begin with an energy assessment.
## A solar-heated house in the town's history

Wikipedia notes that the Dover Sun House, one of the world's first solar-heated houses, was designed in 1948 by architect Eleanor Raymond, with a heating system developed by physicist Mária Telkes. It was demolished in 2010. Today's question is simpler: oil, propane or a heat pump, and which fits your house. See the [Dover page](/cities/dover) for the full picture.

faq.q: Which rebate applies to a Dover heat pump?
faq.a: It follows the utility on your electric bill. A Mass Save sponsor leads to the Mass Save whole-home rebate, and a municipal utility runs its own program. Once you have the name, confirm the current terms at masssave.com or with the utility. A heat pump is also a new electrical load in a house that has run on fuel, so the electrical service is worth raising early.

faq.q: Can a heat pump replace an oil boiler entirely?
faq.a: In some houses, yes, and in others it works alongside a boiler. It depends on the heating load, the insulation and the layout. With 1,347 oil-heated homes in town, many Dover owners face this exact question, and a heating load assessment is the first step toward an answer for any single house.

faq.q: Does a Dover house need weatherization before a rebate?
faq.a: For the whole-home rebate, yes. A house passes by age (2000 or later), by an assessment recommending under $1,000 of work, or by completed recommendations from 2013 or later. Dover's median build year is 1972, so the typical house would start with an assessment rather than pass on age.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Dover is almost entirely owner-occupied, with 94.2% of households owning, and oil is the leading fuel, so the core of a tune-up here is the yearly oil cleaning plus a look at how old the equipment is.
body: ## Almost entirely owner-occupied

Dover counts 1,777 owner-occupied households (94.2%) against 110 renter households (5.8%) in the ACS 2022. With so few rentals, maintenance is mostly a homeowner's call, made one detached house at a time.
## What the fuel decides

- **Oil:** yearly burner and heat-exchanger cleaning, nozzle and filter change, combustion test.
- **Propane or natural gas:** burner, venting and controls checked for safety.
- **Heat pump or mini-split:** coils and filters cleaned, refrigerant side reviewed.
Which of these applies depends on what is in the basement, which is why the nameplate matters.
## A house from the sixties or seventies

About a third of Dover homes went up between 1960 and 1979, and the median year is 1972. Equipment in those houses may have been swapped once already. Leaks, rust, a burner that starts and stops often and fuel use creeping up are the usual signs of age. Catching one in September beats discovering it in January.
## Empty and seasonal houses

Dover counts 68 vacant housing units (3.5%), 26th of 50, close to the 3.6% of the middle town. A heating system in an unoccupied house still needs its fuel level, thermostat and pipes watched through winter, and a check in early fall settles whether the heat will come on.
## The calendar

Heating checks fit late summer or early fall. Cooling checks fit spring, before the first heat wave. Outdoor units need space around them, free of leaves, snow and shrubs. A new noise, a smell or soot near an oil burner is worth a call whatever the month.
## Before the visit

Clear a path to the equipment, replace the filter if it is due, and jot down what you have noticed and when. Fuel type, age and nameplate details speed up the visit. Mass HVAC services homes and businesses; the [heating page](/cities/dover/heating-installation-repair) covers repair and replacement.

faq.q: How often should a Dover oil boiler be cleaned?
faq.a: Once a year, ideally before the heating season. Oil heats 1,347 occupied Dover homes, so this is the most common service call in town. Oil equipment collects soot, and a yearly cleaning keeps the burner running cleanly and may catch a small fault early, before the first cold snap.

faq.q: What should I note before booking a visit?
faq.a: The fuel, the rough age of the equipment, anything unusual you have heard or smelled, and the make and model if the nameplate is readable. If the house has both a main system and a second source such as a mini-split, mention both so each gets looked at.

faq.q: Do propane systems need a yearly visit too?
faq.a: A yearly check is a sensible habit. Bottled or tank gas heats 229 Dover homes, and the burner, venting and controls are what such a visit looks at. A propane house also has a tank and regulator outdoors, so keep the area around them clear of snow, leaves and shrubs.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Dover's houses span several eras: 12.8% date from 1939 or earlier, 9.6% from 1940 to 1959 and 23.5% from 1980 to 1999. Older houses tend to leak more air, tighter ones may need ventilation, and filters and humidity matter in both.
body: ## Old and newer houses breathe differently

According to the ACS 2022, 251 Dover housing units (12.8%) were built in 1939 or earlier, 188 (9.6%) from 1940 to 1959, and 460 (23.5%) from 1980 to 1999. Older houses often leak more air, which brings in outdoor air along with dust, pollen and humidity. Tighter, more recent houses may hold moisture and odors longer, and mechanical ventilation can help them.
## Combustion and fuel

Oil and bottled gas are the leading fuels in Dover. Burners and flues need a yearly check, and a working carbon monoxide alarm covers the basics. Soot, a smell near the burner or a flame that looks wrong are reasons to call.
## Big houses, many rooms

With 1,872 detached houses, Dover has few small apartments where one fan clears the air. A large house can hold different conditions in different wings: a damp basement, a dry upstairs, a bedroom that never gets fresh air. A large house can need more than one fix.
## Where to start

Most air quality complaints begin with a simple observation: a stuffy room, a musty smell, dust that returns quickly, or windows that fog in winter. Each points to a different cause, such as a clogged filter, moisture, poor airflow or too little ventilation. Noting which rooms and which season helps narrow a larger detached house down room by room.
## The usual levers

- A filter that suits the equipment, changed on schedule.
- Humidifiers or dehumidifiers where the air runs very dry or damp.
- Exhaust fans that vent outdoors, and mechanical ventilation in tight houses.
- A look at the ducts, with cleaning only if the inspection justifies it.
Mass HVAC does indoor air quality work for homes and businesses. A fan or a filter is sometimes enough on its own. See the [Dover page](/cities/dover) for the town overview.

faq.q: Does a tight modern house need ventilation?
faq.a: It often benefits from planned ventilation, because air that does not leak out holds moisture and odors. Dover has 402 units built in 2000 or later (20.6%), which are the likeliest to be tight. Exhaust fans that vent outdoors are the simplest start, and mechanical ventilation is the next step.

faq.q: Should I clean the ducts in my Dover house?
faq.a: Only if there is a reason, such as visible dirt, water damage or construction dust. Otherwise regular filter changes are usually the first step. A house with no ducts, such as one heated by radiators, has nothing to clean, and its air quality comes down to fans, humidity and filters on any portable units.

faq.q: Can a mini-split improve air quality in an older Dover room?
faq.a: It can help with temperature and humidity in one room, and its filter catches some dust. It does not bring in fresh air by itself, so a stuffy room may still need an exhaust fan or a ventilation unit. Keep the indoor filter clean, because a clogged one cuts airflow.
